subject.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab

question: Should extension-relay browser routes expose a relay-owned stable public target handle across renderer detach/reattach, or should this PR retain the existing recovery behavior until that owner contract is implemented?
rationale: The safe no-inference principle is clear, but only the relay owner can choose whether raw CDP target replacement remains externally visible or is hidden behind a stable relay handle; the current patch removes recovery without supplying that contract.

options.title: Implement stable relay handles
options.body: Have the relay bridge preserve a public target identity across approved-tab renderer replacement and return that backend-owned outcome to routes.

options.title: Keep recovery temporarily
options.body: Retain the existing relay-specific recovery path until a stable relay-handle implementation and migration contract are ready.

options.title: Accept stale relay targets
options.body: Merge the no-inference change knowing renderer swaps can require callers to rediscover and explicitly reselect the tab.

recommendation.title: Implement stable relay handles
recommendation.body: Have the relay bridge preserve a public target identity across approved-tab renderer replacement and return that backend-owned outcome to routes.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical report and PR discussion assign the unresolved relay identity contract to a browser-owner decision.
